title: Fixed-point number representation
summary: Fixed-point represents real numbers with a fixed number of digits after the radix point. An n-bit fixed-point number with f fractional bits: value = integer / 2^f. Range: -2^(n-f-1) to 2^(n-f-1) - 2^(-f). Common formats: Q15 (16-bit, 15 frac), Q31 (32-bit, 31 frac), Q1.15, Q1.31. Used in DSP, embedded systems, and financial calculations where floating-point is too slow or non-deterministic.

structure.meaning: The whole number part (including sign bit for signed).
Qm.n: m integer bits, n fractional bits, 1 sign bit. Total = m+n+1.
1 sign + 0 integer + 15 fractional. Range: -1.0 to 0.99997. Resolution: 2^-15.
1 sign + 0 integer + 31 fractional. Range: -1.0 to 0.9999999995. Resolution: 2^-31.

notes: Fixed-point is used in DSP (audio processing, filters), embedded systems (no FPU), and financial calculations.
Multiplication of two Qm.n numbers gives Q2m.2n; need to shift right by n to get Qm.n.
Overflow must be handled explicitly (saturation or wraparound).
Fixed-point is deterministic (no rounding mode ambiguity), unlike floating-point.
